mainTopic: פריעה, the fleshy baby, and the ברכות of מילה, followed by the opening of פרק תולין: hanging a wine strainer and the laws of אהל עראי
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה: cutting without פריעה (peeling back the membrane) counts as no מילה at all. רב defines the blocking flesh as flesh covering most of the height of the עטרה. Next, שמואל and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל give mirror-image tests for a fleshy baby, and the גמרא shows that they differ only in an unclear, in-between case. A ברייתא then lists the ברכות said at a ברית: by the מוהל, the father, the people present, and a closing ברכה ending 'כורת הברית', with special versions for גרים and עבדים. After the הדרן, the new פרק תולין begins with a מחלוקת about hanging a wine strainer on יום טוב and שבת. The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר can allow this when he forbids even adding to a temporary tent. It answers that he follows רבי יהודה on מכשירי אוכל נפש, and is even more lenient than him. Finally, רב יוסף rules that, according to the חכמים, someone who hangs the strainer must bring a חטאת. אביי challenges him with the case of a jug hung on a peg, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Cutting without uncovering is no circumcision
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a מילה done without פריעה is treated as if no מילה was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone circumcised but did not uncover the circumcision, it is as if he did not circumcise.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It teaches that cutting the ערלה alone is not enough, and the thin membrane underneath must also be peeled back (פריעה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats פריעה as a required part of the מצוה itself, not an optional extra. Without it, the baby still has the halachic status of not being circumcised. The phrase כאילו לא מל means the whole act is incomplete, not that it was only done imperfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Circumcised (cut the foreskin)
Uncovered, meaning he peeled back the thin membrane under the foreskin (פריעה)
Circumcision
As if he did not circumcise

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that מילה has two required stages: cutting (חיתוך) and uncovering (פריעה).
steps.confusionAlert: פריעה is not the cutting of the foreskin. It is a separate second step, peeling back the thin membrane after the cut.

phrases.english: If one circumcised but did not uncover the circumcision
phrases.notes: פריעה means folding back the thin membrane beneath the foreskin.

phrases.english: it is as if he did not circumcise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the משנה's list of factors that invalidate a מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מילה without פריעה counts as no מילה at all.

steps.title: רב defines the flesh that invalidates the circumcision
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the blocking flesh mentioned in the משנה means flesh covering most of the height of the עטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אבינא said that רבי ירמיה בר אבא said that רב said: It means flesh that covers most of the height of the עטרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining a phrase from earlier in the משנה, which mentioned 'flesh that covers most of the עטרה' as a blocking leftover. רב clarifies which measurement 'most' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think 'most of the עטרה' only means most of its circumference, going around. רב adds that it is measured by height too, so flesh covering most of the height of the עטרה also invalidates the מילה. This defines the term more precisely and does not add a new law.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh that covers
Most, the majority
Its height
The corona (crown) of the organ

steps.confusionAlert: רב is explaining a phrase from earlier in the משנה (the ציצין המעכבין), not the פריעה line that came right before him here.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Avina said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
phrases.notes: A chain of transmission back to רב.

phrases.english: Flesh that covers
most of the height of the corona.
phrases.notes: Explains the משנה's phrase about flesh covering most of the עטרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבִינָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by defining a term from the earlier part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flesh covering most of the height of the עטרה is a blocking leftover that invalidates the מילה.

steps.title: שמואל on examining a fleshy baby
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's case of a fleshy baby, שמואל rules that we examine him when the organ is hard. If he looks circumcised he needs no further מילה, and otherwise he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if he was fleshy, etc.' שמואל said: A child encumbered with flesh, we examine him. As long as when it hardens he looks circumcised, he does not need to be circumcised. And if not, he needs to be circumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a baby with extra flesh, and שמואל gives a practical test: check the baby in a state of hardness to see whether he looks circumcised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the normal state the extra flesh may hide the עטרה, so the baby looks uncircumcised even when the מילה was valid. שמואל rules that the true test is the hardened state. His wording sets the default as 'needs מילה', and the baby is excused only if he clearly looks circumcised.

keyTerms.meaning: Fleshy, having extra flesh
A child encumbered (wrapped up) with flesh
We examine him
Becomes hard (erect)
Circumcised (in appearance)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical halachic test used for a baby whose extra flesh makes him look uncircumcised.

phrases.english: We learned: 'And if he was fleshy, etc.'
phrases.notes: A quote of the משנה's phrase, introducing the discussion.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A child who is encumbered with flesh,
we examine him,
as long as when it hardens he looks circumcised,
he does not need to be circumcised again,
and if not, he needs to be circumcised again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיָה בַּעַל בָּשָׂר וְכוּ׳ אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה (the fleshy baby) and gives שמואל's ruling on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Examine the fleshy child when the organ is hard. If he appears circumcised, no further מילה is needed. If not, he must be circumcised again.

steps.title: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's mirror-image phrasing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל giving the same test as שמואל, but worded from the opposite side. If the baby does not look circumcised he needs מילה, and otherwise he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A child encumbered with flesh, we examine him. As long as when it hardens he does not look circumcised, he needs to be circumcised. And if not, he does not need to be circumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel ruling from a ברייתא that sounds almost identical to שמואל's, but flips the wording. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will ask what practical difference there is between the two phrasings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's default is 'needs מילה' unless the baby clearly looks circumcised. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's default is 'no מילה needed' unless the baby clearly looks uncircumcised. The two only differ in an unclear, in-between case, and that is exactly what the גמרא will explore next.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in it)
And he does not look circumcised
And if not (otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the two opinions are identical. They agree on clear cases, but their opposite defaults lead to different results when the baby's appearance is in doubt.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל both examine the fleshy baby when hard. שמואל requires a clear circumcised look to excuse him, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires a clear uncircumcised look to obligate him.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A child who is encumbered with flesh,
we examine him,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁמִּתְקַשֶּׁה וְאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה מָהוּל —
phrases.english: as long as when it hardens he does not look circumcised,
he needs to be circumcised again,
and if not, he does not need to be circumcised again.
phrases.notes: Mirror image of שמואל's wording, which sets up the question of what difference there is between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא with reversed phrasing, setting up a comparison with שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Examine the fleshy child when hard. If he does not appear circumcised, he must be circumcised again. Otherwise he need not be.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two wordings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between שמואל's wording and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step: if both tests sound the same, when would they give different results?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said that if the baby looks circumcised, he needs nothing more. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that if he does not look circumcised, he needs מילה. These sound like mirror images, so the גמרא wants to know whether the different wording changes the law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: Between שמואל (Step 3) and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (Step 4).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two wordings brought in Steps 3 and 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case would שמואל's wording and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's wording give different rulings?

steps.title: They differ in an in-between case
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions differ when the baby looks partly circumcised and partly not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them in a case where he looks circumcised and also does not look circumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions split over an unclear, in-between case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל needs the baby to clearly look circumcised in order to skip a second מילה, so in an unclear case he needs מילה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires מילה only if the baby clearly looks uncircumcised, so in an unclear case he does not need it. The 'positive' or 'negative' wording decides which way the unclear case goes.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Looks circumcised and also does not look so: an unclear middle case

steps.whatToRemember: An unclear case needs מילה according to שמואל, and does not according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume two opposite wordings of the same test always mean the same thing. The wording decides who wins the unclear middle case.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he looks circumcised and also does not look circumcised

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a borderline case: שמואל requires מילה, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not.

steps.title: Returning to the משנה: circumcised without uncovering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'מל ולא פרע' to open its next discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: He circumcised but did not uncover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the משנה as a heading. It is setting up the next move, a ברייתא about the ברכות of מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only a citation of the משנה's words, not a new ruling. It marks that the גמרא is moving to a new topic connected to this משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Uncovered: did the פְּרִיעָה, peeling back the membrane after cutting

phrases.english: He circumcised but did not uncover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the examination discussion and returns to the משנה's text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A citation heading from the משנה introducing the next ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברכות of the מוהל, the father, and the people present
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists what the מוהל, the father, and the people standing there each say at a ברית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The one who circumcises says, 'Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us about circumcision.' The baby's father says, 'Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us to bring him into the covenant of אברהם our father.' The people standing there say, 'Just as he entered the covenant, so may he enter into Torah, the wedding canopy, and good deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists the ברכות said at a ברית מילה, and who says each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מוהל makes a ברכה on the act of cutting itself (על המילה). The father makes a separate ברכה on his own מצוה of bringing his son into אברהם's covenant. The crowd adds a wish for the child's future: Torah, marriage, and good deeds.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who does the circumcision (the מוֹהֵל)
The father of the baby
To bring him into the covenant of אברהם our father
The people standing there, the crowd
Wedding canopy, meaning marriage

steps.whyThisMatters: These are the ברכות still said at every ברית today.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The one who circumcises says:
"Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us concerning circumcision."
The father of the son says:
"Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us to bring him
into the covenant of Abraham our father."
Those standing there say:
"Just as he entered the covenant,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ יִכָּנֵס לְתוֹרָה לְחוּפָּה וּלְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים״.
phrases.english: so may he enter into Torah, the wedding canopy, and good deeds."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא introduced under the משנה heading of Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מוהל says 'על המילה', the father says 'להכניסו בבריתו של אברהם אבינו', and the crowd responds 'כשם שנכנס לברית'.

steps.title: The closing ברכה: 'Who establishes the covenant'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the text of the extra ברכה that ends with 'כורת הברית'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who makes the ברכה says: 'Who made the beloved one holy from the womb, placed a law in his flesh, and sealed his descendants with the sign of the holy covenant. Therefore, as a reward for this, the living God, our Portion [our Rock], commanded to save the beloved of our flesh from destruction, for the sake of His covenant that He placed in our flesh. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who establishes the covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the longer ברכה, said by one person (usually over a cup of wine), that praises ה׳ for the covenant of מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'beloved one from the womb' refers to a forefather. רש״י says it is יצחק, who was designated for מילה before birth. The ברכה says that in the merit of מילה, ה׳ saves our people from destruction. It ends with a חתימה: 'כורת הברית'.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says the extra ברכה (often over a cup of wine)
Beloved one from the womb (רש״י: יצחק)
His flesh
The sign of the holy covenant
Who establishes (literally 'cuts') the covenant

phrases.english: And the one who blesses says:
"Who made the beloved one holy from the womb,
placed a law in his flesh,
and sealed his descendants with the sign of the holy covenant.
Therefore, as a reward for this,
the living God, our Portion [our Rock],
phrases.notes: The bracket shows a textual variant.

phrases.english: commanded to save the beloved of our flesh from destruction
for the sake of His covenant that He placed in our flesh.
Blessed are You, Lord, Who establishes the covenant."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the closing ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra ברכה is said, ending 'ברוך אתה ה׳ כורת הברית'.

steps.title: The מוהל's ברכה when circumcising converts
steps.stepSummary: When circumcising גרים, the מוהל says the same ברכה 'על המילה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who circumcises converts says: 'Blessed are You, ה׳ our God, King of the universe, Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us concerning circumcision.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new case, circumcising גרים, and gives the מוהל's ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מוהל's ברכה is the same as for a Jewish baby. However, no ברכה of a father is listed here, since there is no Jewish father bringing a son into the covenant.

keyTerms.meaning: One who circumcises converts

phrases.english: One who circumcises converts says:
"Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe,
Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us concerning circumcision,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברכות to a different case: גרים instead of a Jewish baby.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מוהל of a גר says the ordinary 'על המילה' ברכה.

steps.title: The closing ברכה for converts and the power of covenant blood
steps.stepSummary: The closing ברכה for גרים thanks ה׳ for the command to circumcise them and draw covenant blood, which keeps the world in existence.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who makes the ברכה says: 'Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us to circumcise converts and to draw from them covenant blood. For if not for the blood of the covenant, heaven and earth would not last, as it says: "If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth." Blessed are You, ה׳, Who establishes the covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the special closing ברכה said at the מילה of גרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברכה mentions drawing דם ברית from the גר, a step that is essential to his conversion. It brings the פסוק in ירמיהו to show that the covenant of מילה is so important that the world exists because of it. It ends with the same חתימה, 'כורת הברית'.

keyTerms.meaning: To draw a drop of covenant blood
If not for
The laws (order) of heaven and earth

steps.whatToRemember: At a ברית there is the מוהל's ברכה, the father's ברכה, the crowd's response, and a closing ברכה ending 'כורת הברית'. For גרים, the closing ברכה speaks of דם ברית keeping heaven and earth in existence.

phrases.english: And the one who blesses says:
"Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us to circumcise converts
and to draw from them the blood of the covenant,
for were it not for the blood of the covenant,
heaven and earth would not endure,
as it is said:
'If not for My covenant day and night,
the laws of heaven and earth I would not have set.'
Blessed are You, Lord, Who establishes the covenant."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברכות for the מילה of גרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The closing ברכה for גרים mentions drawing דם ברית, quotes the פסוק 'אם לא בריתי', and ends 'כורת הברית'.

steps.title: The ברכה said by the one circumcising slaves
steps.stepSummary: The מוהל of עבדים says the standard ברכה 'על המילה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who circumcises slaves says: 'Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us concerning circumcision.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now moves on from גרים to עבדים. It says that the מוהל of a slave says the same basic ברכה, 'על המילה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This copies the pattern from step 10. The מוהל's own ברכה stays the same whether he is circumcising a baby, a גר, or an עבד. Only the extra closing ברכה changes from case to case.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-Jewish slaves owned by a Jew. They must have a ברית and keep some מצוות.
The one who does the circumcision

phrases.english: One who circumcises slaves says:
"Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us concerning circumcision,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the pattern used for גרים in step 10 to the case of עבדים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מוהל of עבדים says 'על המילה'.

steps.title: The closing ברכה for circumcising slaves
steps.stepSummary: The מברך thanks ה׳ for the command to circumcise slaves and draw covenant blood, which keeps the world in existence.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the extra ברכה says: 'Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us to circumcise slaves and to draw covenant blood from them. If not for the blood of the covenant, the laws of heaven and earth would not last, as it says: "If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth." Blessed are You, ה׳, Who makes the covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the wording of the extra ברכה for עבדים. It is the same as the one for גרים, except that it says 'עבדים' instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the ברכה for גרים in step 11, this ברכה rests on the פסוק from ירמיהו: the world stands because of the ברית. It ends 'כורת הברית'. That ending matches the general ברכה we saw in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The person who says the extra closing ברכה
To draw out a drop of covenant blood
The fixed laws of heaven and earth (the order of nature)

steps.whatToRemember: For every kind of ברית (baby, גר, עבד), the מוהל says 'על המילה'. The extra ברכה is worded for each case, and every version ends 'כורת הברית'.

phrases.english: And the one who recites the blessing says:
"Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us to circumcise the slaves
and to drip from them covenantal blood,
for were it not for the blood of the covenant,
the laws of heaven and earth would not endure,
as it is said: 'If not for My covenant day and night,
the laws of heaven and earth I would not have set.'
Blessed are You, Lord, Who makes the covenant."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the closing ברכה that goes with the מוהל's ברכה from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra ברכה for עבדים mentions circumcising slaves and covenant blood, and ends 'כורת הברית'.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק רבי אליעזר דמילה
steps.stepSummary: The פרק about מילה on שבת ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק רבי אליעזר דמילה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the הדרן line that marks the end of the פרק. No legal discussion happens here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a formula said on finishing a פרק, expressing the hope to come back to it and learn it again. The next line starts a brand-new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you.' This formula is said on finishing a פרק.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not connect the next משנה's 'רבי אליעזר' to this title. The new פרק is about straining wine, not מילה.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
[chapter] 'Rabbi Eliezer of Circumcision'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole פרק, which on this amud includes steps 1 to 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק on מילה is complete.

steps.title: New פרק: hanging a wine strainer on יום טוב and שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר allows hanging a strainer on יום טוב and pouring through an already-hung one on שבת. חכמים forbid both, but allow pouring through a hung strainer on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: one may hang the strainer on יום טוב, and one may pour into a strainer that is already hanging on שבת. The חכמים say: one may not hang the strainer on יום טוב, and one may not pour into a hanging strainer on שבת. But one may pour into a hanging strainer on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The first משנה of the new פרק (פרק תולין) brings a מחלוקת about stretching a cloth strainer over a vessel to filter wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה covers two actions: hanging the strainer, and pouring wine through a strainer that is already up. רבי אליעזר is lenient on both. On יום טוב he allows even hanging it, and on שבת he allows pouring (which implies hanging is forbidden on שבת). חכמים forbid hanging on יום טוב and forbid pouring on שבת. They allow only pouring on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We hang / suspend.' This is also the name of the new פרק.
A cloth strainer for filtering the dregs out of wine
A strainer that is already hanging (it was set up before)
Festival day, when work for food preparation is partly allowed

steps.confusionAlert: Read the two halves of each opinion carefully. 'Hanging' (תולין) and 'pouring into a hanging one' (נותנין לתלויה) are two different actions, and each opinion rules on them differently for יום טוב and for שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One may hang the strainer on a Festival,
and one may pour into a hanging one on Shabbat.
And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תּוֹלִין אֶת הַמְשַׁמֶּרֶת בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not hang the strainer on a Festival,
and one may not pour into a hanging one on Shabbat,
but one may pour into a hanging one on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: תּוֹלִין אֶת הַמְשַׁמֶּרֶת בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק with a completely new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: hanging is allowed on יום טוב, and pouring is allowed on שבת. חכמים: no hanging on יום טוב and no pouring on שבת, but pouring is allowed on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of פרק תולין, which deals with preparing food and drink on שבת and יום טוב without doing forbidden kinds of making.

steps.title: How can רבי אליעזר allow making a tent?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר forbids even adding to a temporary tent, so how can he allow making one from scratch by hanging a strainer?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, רבי אליעזר says we may not even add to a temporary tent. Would he allow making one from the start?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's lenient ruling in the משנה, because it seems to clash with his strict view elsewhere about temporary tents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stretching a strainer over a vessel makes a kind of covering, which counts as an אהל עראי (temporary tent). Elsewhere רבי אליעזר forbids even adding to such a tent on a day of rest. So it is strange that he allows building one from the start here. The גמרא will next explain where that strict view of his comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary tent or covering, forbidden to set up on שבת and יום טוב (מדרבנן)
To add on (to something that already exists)
From the start, in the first place
'Now,' meaning: since this is so. It opens a קל וחומר style challenge.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Now, Rabbi Eliezer,
[holds] we may not even add to a temporary tent,
is making one in the first place permitted?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹסוֹפֵי אֹהֶל עֲרַאי לָא מוֹסְפִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אליעזר's lenient ruling about hanging the strainer on יום טוב in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's permission to hang the strainer (תולין את המשמרת) on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if adding to a temporary tent is forbidden, then making one from scratch should be even more forbidden. Hanging a strainer is like making a tent.

steps.title: Source for the challenge: the window shutter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה about a window shutter. This is the source for the claim that רבי אליעזר forbids adding to a temporary tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source? As we learned in a משנה: a window shutter. רבי אליעזר says: when it is tied on and hanging, one may close the window with it. If not, one may not close the window with it. The חכמים say: either way, one may close the window with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up its challenge from Step 16 by showing where we learn that רבי אליעזר is strict about tents. It quotes a משנה about closing a window with a shutter on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Closing a window with a shutter is like adding to a structure. רבי אליעזר allows it only if the shutter is already tied and hanging, because then it is clearly part of the house's equipment. The חכמים allow it either way. This משנה by itself does not yet prove the tent rule. רבי יוחנן's explanation in the next step completes the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for the source of a claim)
A window shutter or plug used to close a window
Tied on and hanging
One may close or plug (the window)

phrases.english: What is it (the source)?
As we learned in a Mishnah: a window shutter,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
When it is tied on and hanging,
one may close the window with it,
and if not, one may not close the window with it.
And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ — פּוֹקְקִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Either way, one may close the window with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the premise of the challenge in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי אליעזר forbids adding to a temporary tent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a window shutter (פקק החלון).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the dispute is only about adding to a tent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that everyone agrees a new temporary tent may not be made on יום טוב or שבת. The argument is only about adding to one. רבי אליעזר forbids adding even on יום טוב, and the חכמים permit it even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that one may not make a temporary tent from scratch on יום טוב, and certainly not on שבת. They argue only about adding to one. רבי אליעזר says: one may not add on יום טוב, and certainly not on שבת. The חכמים say: one may add on שבת, and certainly on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains what the shutter argument is really about. This completes the source for the challenge in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Closing a window with a shutter counts as 'adding' to a temporary tent. So רבי אליעזר's strictness in the משנה shows he forbids adding, even on יום טוב. If he forbids merely adding, how can he allow hanging a strainer, which makes a tent from scratch? That is the full force of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
A temporary tent or covering
From scratch; at the start
To add to an existing structure
Needless to say; all the more so

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the two sides use 'needless to say' in opposite directions. רבי אליעזר goes from יום טוב (forbidden) to שבת (certainly forbidden). The חכמים go from שבת (permitted) to יום טוב (certainly permitted).
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation turns the window-shutter משנה into proof that רבי אליעזר is strict about tents even on יום טוב. That is exactly what makes his lenient strainer ruling hard to understand.

phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Everyone agrees that one may not make
a temporary tent from scratch on a Festival,
and needless to say, on Shabbat.
They disagreed only about adding,
as Rabbi Eliezer says:
One may not add on a Festival,
and needless to say, on Shabbat.
And the Rabbis say: One may add on Shabbat,
and needless to say, on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה from Step 17, turning it into the proof behind the challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a new temporary tent is forbidden by everyone. רבי אליעזר forbids even adding to one on יום טוב, while the חכמים permit adding even on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר follows רבי יהודה on food-preparation tools
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר follows רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה permits on יום טוב even the actions that prepare the tools for making food, so hanging a strainer for wine is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds like רבי יהודה. As a ברייתא teaches: the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation. רבי יהודה permits even the preparations that make food-making possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Hanging a strainer would normally be a forbidden tent, but רבי אליעזר allows it on יום טוב because it serves food preparation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only actual food-making (אוכל נפש) is allowed on יום טוב. רבי יהודה goes further and also allows preparing the tools used for food (מכשירי אוכל נפש). Hanging a strainer prepares the tool for straining wine to drink on יום טוב. That explains why it is allowed on יום טוב but not on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds like (follows the opinion of)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Food preparation (work needed to make food)
Preparations that enable food-making, like readying the tools

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not deny that hanging a strainer is a tent. He agrees it is normally forbidden. He permits it on יום טוב only because it serves food preparation.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds like Rabbi Yehuda.
As it was taught in a baraita:
There is no difference between a Festival and Shabbat
except food preparation alone.
Rabbi Yehuda permits
even the preparations that enable food-making.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built in Steps 16 to 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the opinion to another תנא's principle (רבי יהודה on מכשירי אוכל נפש).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי אליעזר forbids even adding to a tent, he should certainly forbid hanging a strainer.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hanging a strainer is a tent, but on יום טוב it is permitted as a preparation for food, following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: But a strainer could have been hung before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. רבי יהודה may permit only preparations that could not have been done before יום טוב, and a strainer could easily have been hung the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that we heard רבי יהודה permits preparations that could not have been done on ערב יום טוב. But preparations that could have been done on ערב יום טוב — did you ever hear him permit those?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 19. It argues that רבי יהודה's leniency may be too narrow to cover the strainer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's leniency may be limited to tool preparations that truly could not be done before the holiday. Hanging a strainer is something one could do on ערב יום טוב. So we have no proof that רבי יהודה would permit it, and the comparison to רבי אליעזר seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Say that we heard him (rule this way); granted he said that much
Impossible
The day before the Festival
Did you hear him say that? (rhetorical: no)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important distinction in the laws of יום טוב: tool preparations that could have been done before the holiday versus ones that could not. The answer, which comes next, is that רבי אליעזר is even more lenient than רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Say that we heard Rabbi Yehuda permit
preparations that are impossible
to do on the eve of the Festival;
but preparations that are possible
to do on the eve of the Festival,
did you hear him permit them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר's strainer ruling follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's leniency may apply only to preparations that could not have been done before יום טוב. A strainer could have been hung on ערב יום טוב, so his view does not clearly cover it.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר is even more lenient than רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 20. רבי אליעזר goes further than רבי יהודה and permits even preparations that could have been done before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The view of רבי אליעזר goes further than that of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20 by sharpening its earlier answer. רבי אליעזר shares רבי יהודה's approach but is even more lenient, so he allows hanging the strainer even though it could have been done the day before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 pointed out that רבי יהודה may only allow food preparations that could not be done before יום טוב. The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר's view is a stronger version of רבי יהודה's view: he allows food-related preparations on יום טוב even when they could have been done earlier. That explains why he permits hanging the strainer.

keyTerms.meaning: goes further / is stronger (here: more lenient)
preparations for making food, such as readying the tools
the day before יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, רבי אליעזר permits hanging the strainer because he allows food preparations on יום טוב even if they could have been done beforehand. He goes further than רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 18. There רבי אליעזר was the strict one about adding to a tent. Here he is the lenient one about preparing food tools. These are two different areas of law.

phrases.english: That [the view] of Rabbi Eliezer
goes further than that of Rabbi Yehudah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by widening רבי אליעזר's leniency beyond רבי יהודה's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a position: רבי אליעזר holds a stronger leniency than the source he was linked to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר only matches רבי יהודה, who may permit only preparations that could not be done before יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר permits food preparations even when they could have been done before יום טוב.

steps.title: According to the Rabbis, what if someone did hang the strainer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים of the משנה, who forbid hanging the strainer, and asks what the law is if someone hung it anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And the חכמים say' that one may not hang it. The question was asked: if a person did hang it, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the other opinion in the משנה, the חכמים, and asks how serious it is if someone hung the strainer anyway. This sets up a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say hanging the strainer is forbidden, but they do not say how serious the prohibition is. The גמרא wants to know whether it is a Torah-level violation or only a rabbinic one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and the Sages say', a quote from the משנה
'they asked': an open question raised in the בית המדרש
he hung (it)

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] And the Rabbis say [one may not hang it].
A question was raised before them:
If he hung it, what [is the law]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי אליעזר's view and opens a new question about the חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How severe is it, according to the חכמים, if someone actually hung the strainer? Is it a Torah violation or a rabbinic one?

steps.title: רב יוסף: hanging the strainer requires a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that someone who hangs the strainer by mistake must bring a חטאת. That means it is a Torah-level act of making a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: if he hung it, he must bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. Hanging the strainer is a real Torah violation, so someone who does it by mistake must bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is brought only for a Torah-level מלאכה done by mistake. So רב יוסף treats the hanging strainer as a real tent, which counts as building.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא, the teacher of אביי
must bring a sin-offering, which applies to a Torah violation done by mistake

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If he hung it, he is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: תָּלָה חַיָּיב חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a Torah violation (making a tent), so a mistaken act requires a חטאת.

steps.title: אביי: then hanging a jug on a peg would also make one liable
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. If hanging something counts as making a tent, then hanging a jug on a peg should make a person liable too, and that sounds ridiculous.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: if so, a person who hangs a jug on a peg should also be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer by comparing it to an everyday case: hanging a jug on a peg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If simply hanging something up counted as building a tent, then hanging a jug on a peg would also be a Torah violation. Everyone knows that cannot be right. So אביי argues that just hanging an object cannot be enough to count as building a tent.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא, the student of רב יוסף
'but if so': this introduces an argument that the view leads to an absurd result
a jug
a peg

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if that is so,
if one hung a jug on a peg,
is he also liable?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that hanging the strainer is a Torah violation requiring a חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Argument from absurdity: if hanging alone counts as making a tent, then hanging a jug on a peg would also be a Torah violation, which is obviously false.
